recommended_actions.title: Verify .NET target, package and operating-system support
recommended_actions.rationale: Static references and declarations require independent deployment and interoperability checks; missing versions remain unknown.
steps: Deployed runtime, OS, provider and native backend versions are unknown. Target frameworks, global.json SDK selection and NuGet package declarations are separate source claims, not the installed runtime.

.NET 10 documents MLKem, MLDsa and SlhDsa. Check the selected parameter, OS/backend support and IsSupported or IsAlgorithmSupported in the deployed environment; Linux facilities may require OpenSSL 3.5 or later. Do not generalize platform support across Windows, Linux and macOS.

.NET 11 CompositeMLKem and Hpke facilities require review of the exact API and experimental diagnostics. HPKE alone does not identify a PQC KEM. Check Bouncy Castle package/version independently of the .NET target.

ASP.NET/Kestrel TLS depends on the OS/TLS backend and peer negotiation; cryptographic API availability does not enable PQC TLS. Data Protection AES payloads are not a reason to replace symmetric encryption with a KEM.

recommended_actions.title: Track PQC readiness of dependent libraries
recommended_actions.rationale: Dependency-level crypto libraries strongly influence migration options and operational timelines.
steps: Record current versions in dependency-sbom.json and define upgrade targets.
Subscribe to release notes for PQC feature availability and API changes.
Run integration tests for PQC or hybrid modes before promoting to production.

findings.description: PHP cryptographic API or library reference; key type may be unresolved.
findings.migration_hint: Review the resolved primitive and purpose; PHP source alone does not establish loaded extensions, key type or active use.

recommended_actions.title: Verify PHP extensions and their native cryptographic backends
recommended_actions.rationale: Static references and declarations require independent deployment and interoperability checks; missing versions remain unknown.
steps: Deployed PHP, extension and native library versions are unknown from a source or manifest reference. Composer config.platform is emulated dependency resolution, not the deployed PHP version.
PHP 8.6 Sodium KEM APIs require libsodium 1.0.22 or later. Keep X-Wing separate from pure ML-KEM-768 and TLS hybrid groups; confirm the actual loaded extension and operation.
Check ext-pqcrypto and paragonie/pqcrypto_compat independently; a Composer package is not a native extension. Verify each documented algorithm, version and maintenance/audit status.

For PHP OpenSSL calls, verify the linked OpenSSL/provider and exposed PHP API. OpenSSL PQC primitives alone do not establish PHP KEM or TLS support. Framework encryption using AES does not call for blanket replacement with a public-key KEM.

recommended_actions.title: Introduce crypto abstraction boundary for algorithm agility
recommended_actions.rationale: Direct algorithm calls create high migration cost. A boundary layer enables staged classical-to-PQC transitions.
steps: Wrap signing, verification, keygen, and key exchange behind stable interfaces.
Add policy controls to select classical, hybrid, or PQC paths at runtime.

recommended_actions.title: Verify C/C++ library, provider and build capabilities
recommended_actions.rationale: Static references and declarations require independent deployment and interoperability checks; missing versions remain unknown.
steps: The deployed native library, build options, provider configuration and peer capabilities are unknown. vcpkg/Conan declarations, baselines and CMake references are not installed libraries or a reconstructed build graph.

OpenSSL 3.5 supplies ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in its default provider; oqsprovider is not required for every OpenSSL PQC use. Check the exact OpenSSL build, enabled algorithms and provider/property selection.

For liboqs, liboqs-cpp and oqsprovider, verify separate compatible versions, disabled/enabled algorithms, native build flags and maintenance status. OQS integrations are prototypes; a wrapper/include reference does not establish deployment suitability.

TLS groups and provider loads are requested configuration only. Verify peers, negotiated groups, authentication signatures and protocol compatibility independently. Preserve appropriate symmetric encryption rather than replacing AES wholesale with a public-key KEM.
